serviceTranslations.heroDescription: Some mental health conditions require the depth of assessment, diagnostic rigour, and therapeutic range that only a specialist psychiatrist can provide. Treatment-resistant depression, bipolar disorder, adult ADHD, complex anxiety disorders, or any condition that has not responded to GP-level management — these presentations require specialist psychiatry. Our psychiatrists, specialist doctors with MIR psychiatric training, registered with the Spanish Medical Council (OMC — Organización Médica Colegial) and their specialist college, offer specialist psychiatric assessments by secure video call. Same day, from anywhere in Spain, in English, Spanish, or Portuguese.
serviceTranslations.detailBody:
GP Mental Health Assessment vs. Specialist Psychiatric Consultation

Global Health offers two levels of mental health care.

GP mental health assessment — appropriate for initial screening of anxiety, mild to moderate depression, stress, and burnout. The GP conducts a structured assessment, provides clinical recommendations at GP level, and refers to psychiatry where indicated. The right starting point for most initial mental health concerns.

Specialist psychiatric consultation — conducted by Global Health's specialist psychiatrists. Appropriate for:

  • Formal diagnosis of complex mental health disorders
  • Conditions that have not responded to GP-level treatment
  • Bipolar disorder — assessment, diagnosis, and specialist treatment plan
  • Adult ADHD — formal diagnostic assessment and treatment
  • Treatment-resistant depression
  • Complex or refractory anxiety disorders
  • Eating disorders — psychiatric assessment and treatment plan coordination
  • Psychiatric assessment for clinical, occupational, or medico-legal reports
  • Specialist psychiatric second opinion

Not sure which level of support is right for you? Start with the GP mental health assessment — if your presentation requires specialist psychiatric input, your GP refers you directly to this service within the same platform.

Who This Service Is For

This specialist psychiatric consultation is appropriate for adults with:

  • Moderate to severe depression — particularly treatment-resistant, melancholic, or atypical depression
  • Bipolar disorder — diagnostic assessment, treatment plan review, or second opinion
  • Complex anxiety disorders — panic disorder, OCD, severe social anxiety, PTSD
  • Adult ADHD — formal diagnostic assessment, treatment initiation, or review
  • Personality spectrum disorders — assessment and care plan guidance
  • Eating disorders — psychiatric assessment and treatment plan coordination
  • Severe chronic insomnia — when the cause is psychiatric or treatment has failed at GP level
  • Mental health conditions that have not responded to GP-level treatment
  • Psychiatric assessment for occupational, disability, or medico-legal reports
  • Specialist psychiatric second opinion — on a diagnosis, treatment plan, or medication received from another psychiatrist
  • International residents and expats who need specialist psychiatric care in English or Portuguese

What This Service Is — And What It Is Not

This specialist psychiatric consultation is appropriate for:

  • Formal psychiatric diagnosis of complex disorders
  • Specialist psychiatric pharmacological treatment assessment and planning — at the specialist's discretion
  • Psychopharmacological therapy and ongoing psychiatric follow-up
  • Assessment for clinical, occupational, or medico-legal reports
  • Specialist psychiatric second opinion
  • Coordination with clinical psychology, social work, and other services where indicated

This service is not appropriate for:

  • Crisis intervention — if you are in crisis, use the resources at the top of this page
  • Psychiatric admission — involuntary admission is regulated by Article 763 of the Spanish Civil Procedure Act and requires judicial authorisation. It cannot be initiated or coordinated through this service
  • Assessment of acute severe psychosis — where patient safety requires urgent in-person assessment
  • Psychotherapy or psychological therapy — this is a medical psychiatric assessment and treatment service, not a psychotherapy service

Not sure whether you need psychiatry or psychology? Psychiatry is a medical specialty — the psychiatrist assesses, diagnoses, and can prescribe psychiatric medication. The clinical psychologist provides psychotherapy. For many conditions, both work together. Your psychiatrist advises on the most appropriate level of support and can guide you on the type of psychotherapy best suited to your condition.

Conditions Commonly Assessed

Mood disorders

  • Major depressive disorder — including treatment-resistant, melancholic, and atypical depression
  • Bipolar depression — differential diagnosis and specialist treatment plan
  • Bipolar disorder type I and type II — diagnostic assessment, stabilisation, and follow-up
  • Cyclothymic disorder
  • Dysthymia / persistent depressive disorder

Anxiety disorders

  • Panic disorder — with and without agoraphobia
  • Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)
  • Social anxiety disorder — severe or refractory presentations
  • Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)
  • Treatment-resistant generalised anxiety disorder
  • Specific phobia with significant functional impact

Adult ADHD

  • Formal diagnostic assessment of ADHD in adults
  • ADHD with comorbidities — anxiety, depression, sleep disorders
  • Initiation, adjustment, and review of ADHD pharmacological treatment
  • Previously undiagnosed childhood ADHD — adult assessment

Personality spectrum disorders

  • Formal diagnostic assessment of personality disorders
  • Borderline personality disorder — assessment and care plan guidance
  • Narcissistic, avoidant, dependent, and other personality disorders

Eating disorders

  • Anorexia nervosa — psychiatric assessment and treatment plan coordination
  • Bulimia nervosa — assessment and treatment plan
  • Binge eating disorder — assessment and management

Note: severe eating disorders requiring urgent medical nutritional intervention or inpatient admission require in-person assessment. Your psychiatrist assesses severity and advises on the appropriate level of care.

Psychotic disorders — limited assessment

  • Assessment of mild or stably remitted psychotic symptoms
  • Second opinion on diagnosis of schizophrenia or other psychotic disorders in stable patients
  • Antipsychotic medication review in stable patients with known psychosis

Acute psychotic episodes require urgent in-person assessment. This service is not appropriate for the assessment of acute severe psychosis — call 112 or go to the emergency department immediately.

Sleep disorders

  • Severe chronic insomnia — psychiatric assessment and treatment plan
  • Sleep disorders with significant psychiatric basis

Psychiatric assessments for reports

  • Psychiatric reports for temporary or permanent occupational disability
  • Reports for medico-legal processes — at the specialist's discretion
  • Mental health assessments for administrative purposes

What Your Consultation Includes

Complete specialist psychiatric assessment

Your psychiatrist conducts a structured and comprehensive psychiatric assessment — covering your detailed psychiatric history, previous episodes, previous treatments and their response, family history of mental health conditions, current life situation, occupational and social functioning, substance use, and mental state at the time of the consultation.

Formal psychiatric diagnosis

Where the assessment allows, your psychiatrist establishes a formal psychiatric diagnosis based on current international diagnostic criteria — DSM-5-TR or ICD-11 — clearly explained with the clinical reasoning behind it.

Specialist treatment plan

Based on the assessment and diagnosis, your psychiatrist designs a specialist treatment plan — which may include psychotherapy recommendations and guidance on the most appropriate approach for your condition, psychiatric pharmacological treatment options at the specialist's discretion, coordination with clinical psychology or other services where indicated, and structured psychiatric follow-up.

Specialist clinical documentation — at the specialist's discretion

When clinically indicated, your psychiatrist issues appropriate clinical documentation.

Note on benzodiazepines and controlled psychiatric medications: benzodiazepines and certain psychiatric medications are controlled substances in Spain with specific prescribing requirements. Your psychiatrist advises during the consultation on the options available and any applicable limitations.

Safety assessment

Every psychiatric consultation includes a structured safety assessment — conducted with sensitivity as a standard component of specialist care.

Ongoing psychiatric follow-up

Psychiatric treatment is a long-term process. Specialist follow-up consultations are available to monitor treatment response, adjust medication where needed, and provide the clinical continuity that quality psychiatric care requires.

Accessing Psychiatry in Spain — The Reality

Public psychiatry in Spain is under significant pressure — waiting times for a first SNS psychiatrist appointment are measured in months in most autonomous communities. Private in-person psychiatry in Spain is expensive and concentrated in major cities.

For international residents who need specialist psychiatry in English or Portuguese, options are practically non-existent outside Madrid and Barcelona — and even there, availability is very limited.

This service provides access to specialist psychiatry by video call — same day — from anywhere in Spain. For patients who most need psychiatric support, removing the access barrier matters.

Confidentiality in Psychiatric Care

Everything discussed during your psychiatric consultation is confidential and protected under Spanish and European data protection law — including Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) implemented through Organic Law 3/2018 (LOPDGDD) and Law 41/2002 on patient autonomy.

Mental health data has reinforced protection as a special category of data under the GDPR.

There are two circumstances in which confidentiality may need to be carefully considered — when there is serious and immediate risk to your life or safety, or when there is serious risk to the safety of another person. Your psychiatrist discusses confidentiality with you at the outset of the consultation.

Our clinical psychologists, registered with the Colegio Oficial de Psicólogos, offer psychotherapy and psychological assessment by secure video call — in English, Spanish, or Portuguese. No months-long waiting list. No travelling to a clinic when you are already struggling. A registered clinical psychologist, available the same day, from anywhere in Spain.
serviceTranslations.detailBody:
What This Service Is — And What It Is Not

This clinical psychology service includes:

  • Individual psychotherapy — structured, evidence-based psychological intervention
  • Psychological assessment — formal assessment of psychological difficulties and report where indicated
  • Collaborative work with the Global Health psychiatrist where a combined psychotherapy and pharmacology approach is appropriate
  • Psychological guidance for family members of people experiencing psychological difficulties — where indicated
  • Psychotherapy in English or Portuguese for international residents and expats

This service does not include:

  • Medication prescribing — clinical psychologists do not prescribe in Spain. If you need pharmacological assessment, our specialist psychiatry service is appropriate
  • Crisis intervention — if you are in crisis, use the resources at the top of this page
  • Couple or family therapy — this service is individual psychology
  • Forensic or medico-legal psychological assessments — please enquire directly about availability

Not sure whether you need psychology or psychiatry? The practical distinction is straightforward: if you want to talk in depth about what is happening and learn psychological tools to manage it, psychology is the right starting point. If you think medication may be part of the solution, or if you are already taking psychiatric medication and want someone to manage it, psychiatry is more appropriate. For many people, both working together is the most effective approach.

Who This Service Is For

This clinical psychology consultation is appropriate for adults with:

  • Anxiety — generalised anxiety disorder, social anxiety, panic attacks, health anxiety
  • Depression — low mood, loss of interest, mild to moderate depression
  • Stress and burnout — work-related stress, emotional exhaustion, work-life difficulties
  • Trauma and PTSD — past or recent traumatic experiences that continue to affect daily functioning
  • Grief — loss of a loved one, loss of a relationship or significant life role
  • Relationship difficulties — relational patterns that cause distress or conflict
  • Low self-esteem and self-criticism — negative thought patterns about oneself
  • OCD — obsessive-compulsive disorder, intrusive thoughts, compulsions
  • Phobias — specific fears with impact on daily functioning
  • Adjustment difficulties — moving country, job change, relationship breakdown, significant life changes
  • Expat stress — cultural adjustment, isolation, identity, family separation
  • Adult ADHD — psychological support and management strategies for adults with established diagnosis
  • Sleep disorders with significant psychological basis
  • Eating and body image concerns — non-severe presentations
  • Anyone seeking structured psychological support to improve wellbeing and functioning

Therapeutic Approaches

Psychotherapy is not a generic conversation — it is structured, evidence-based psychological intervention. The therapeutic approaches our clinical psychologists use include:

Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT)

The approach with the strongest scientific evidence for most anxiety disorders and depression. Works on the relationship between thoughts, emotions, and behaviours — identifying thought patterns that generate distress and developing more adaptive strategies.

Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)

A third-generation approach working on psychological flexibility — learning to relate differently to difficult thoughts and emotions, and acting in line with personal values even in the presence of distress.

EMDR — Eye Movement Desensitisation and Reprocessing

The treatment with the strongest evidence for trauma and PTSD. Helps the brain process traumatic memories that have become blocked, reducing their emotional impact.

Dialectical Behaviour Therapy (DBT)

Particularly useful for difficulties in emotional regulation, borderline personality disorder, and self-destructive behaviours. Works on mindfulness skills, distress tolerance, emotional regulation, and interpersonal effectiveness.

Brief Psychodynamic Psychotherapy

Useful when current difficulties have roots in past experiences and relational patterns. Works on the meaning of symptoms and deeper understanding of recurring patterns.

Mindfulness-based approaches

Integrated into several therapeutic frameworks, particularly useful for stress, anxiety, and burnout.

The most appropriate therapeutic approach for you depends on your presentation, your goals, and your preferences. Your psychologist discusses this with you in the first consultation and adapts the approach to your specific situation.

What Your First Consultation Includes

Initial psychological assessment

The first consultation is an assessment — your psychologist listens in depth to your situation, understands the impact on your daily functioning, explores relevant personal history, and establishes with you the goals of the therapeutic work.

Clinical formulation

At the end of the first consultation, your psychologist provides an initial formulation — a clinical understanding of what is happening, what factors are contributing, and how the therapeutic work can help.

Therapeutic plan

Your psychologist proposes a therapeutic plan — including the most appropriate approach for your presentation, the recommended session frequency, and the therapeutic objectives to work towards.

Coordination with psychiatry where indicated

Where a combined psychotherapy and pharmacology approach is appropriate, your psychologist coordinates with our specialist psychiatry service within the same platform — so you do not need to start from scratch with each professional.

How Online Therapy Works

Video call psychotherapy has solid and comparable scientific evidence to in-person therapy for most presentations. The therapeutic alliance — the relationship between patient and psychologist, one of the most important factors in therapy outcome — develops equally effectively in the online format.

Practical advantages of online psychotherapy:

  • No travel — consult from the space where you feel most comfortable
  • No waiting room — greater privacy
  • Easier to maintain regularity — sessions are not lost due to scheduling conflicts or travel
  • Access from anywhere in Spain — no geographical limitation
  • Especially useful for expats and international residents — no limitation by language or location

For an effective video session

  • Find a private space where no one can hear you
  • Ensure a stable internet connection
  • Use headphones if possible — improves privacy and sound quality
  • Reserve the full session time — without interruptions

Psychology in Spain — The Access Gap

Clinical psychology in the Spanish public system is significantly under-resourced. In most autonomous communities, the number of psychologists in the SNS is well below the European average — approximately 6 psychologists per 100,000 inhabitants compared to a European average of 18. Waiting times to access SNS clinical psychology are months — where access exists at all.

Private in-person psychology in Spain is expensive in major cities and limited outside them. For international residents who need psychotherapy in English, options narrow dramatically.

This service provides access to clinical psychology by video call — same day for the first consultation — from anywhere in Spain, in English, Spanish, or Portuguese.

Confidentiality

Everything discussed during your psychology sessions is strictly confidential and protected under Spanish and European data protection law — including Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) implemented through Organic Law 3/2018 (LOPDGDD), Law 41/2002 on patient autonomy, and the Psychologist's Code of Ethics.

Mental health data has reinforced protection as a special category under the GDPR.

There are two circumstances in which confidentiality may need to be carefully considered — when there is serious and immediate risk to your life or safety, or when there is serious risk to the safety of another person. Your psychologist discusses confidentiality with you at the outset of the first session.

serviceTranslations.heroDescription: Cardiac concerns — palpitations you do not know how to interpret, an ECG with findings nobody has explained clearly, hypertension that is not well controlled, or an established heart condition requiring specialist review — need the depth of analysis that a specialist cardiologist provides. Our cardiologists, specialist doctors with MIR cardiology training, registered with the Spanish Medical Council (OMC — Organización Médica Colegial) and their specialist college, offer specialist cardiology consultations by secure video call with test review — ECG, echocardiogram, Holter, and other cardiological investigations interpreted by a specialist the same day. From anywhere in Spain, in English, Spanish, or Portuguese.
serviceTranslations.detailBody:
Who This Service Is For

This specialist cardiology consultation is appropriate for adults with:

  • Palpitations — assessment of non-urgent palpitations, perceived heart rhythm irregularity, or ectopic beats
  • An ECG with findings that have not been clearly explained — specialist review and interpretation
  • An echocardiogram, Holter, or stress test report needing specialist explanation
  • Hypertension that is resistant or not well controlled with current medication
  • Known and stable atrial fibrillation — specialist review and ongoing management
  • Stable heart failure — specialist review and treatment optimisation
  • Dyslipidaemia with elevated cardiovascular risk — cardiological risk assessment and management
  • Non-urgent exertional breathlessness — cardiological cause assessment
  • Non-urgent syncope or pre-syncope — cardiological assessment
  • Specialist cardiology second opinion — on a diagnosis, treatment plan, or test result
  • Review of cardiological medication — efficacy, tolerability, and adjustment
  • Cardiovascular risk assessment — particularly in patients with multiple risk factors
  • International residents and expats who need specialist cardiology in English or Portuguese

What This Service Is — And What It Is Not

This specialist cardiology consultation covers:

  • Specialist cardiological assessment of non-urgent presentations
  • Review and interpretation of ECG, echocardiogram, Holter, and other cardiological tests
  • Ongoing management of stable cardiovascular conditions
  • Cardiovascular risk assessment and risk reduction planning
  • Requests for cardiological investigations where clinically indicated
  • Specialist cardiological second opinion
  • Coordination of in-person referral where indicated

This service does not cover:

  • Cardiac emergencies — acute chest pain, syncope with loss of consciousness, severe difficulty breathing, palpitations with haemodynamic compromise. For any acute cardiac symptom, call 112 immediately
  • Interventional cardiology — catheterisation, pacemaker or defibrillator implantation, ablation, cardiac surgery. These procedures require in-person hospital assessment
  • Performing tests — the cardiologist can interpret tests already performed and request new ones, but cannot perform ECG, echocardiogram, or stress testing directly. These require in-person attendance

Not sure whether your symptom is urgent? When in doubt, always call 112 or go to the emergency department. It is always better to be assessed and reassured than to wait.

Cardiological Test Review — How It Works

One of the most valuable capabilities of this service is specialist review and interpretation of cardiological tests by a cardiologist — the same day, without waiting weeks for an in-person specialist appointment.

ECG (Electrocardiogram)

Send the PDF or image of your ECG before the consultation. Your cardiologist interprets it in full — identifying the rhythm, axis, intervals, and any findings of rhythm disturbance, conduction abnormality, or ischaemia — and explains the findings clearly.

Echocardiogram

Send your echocardiogram report. Your cardiologist reviews the ejection fraction, valvular function, cavity dimensions, and any clinically relevant findings — and explains what they mean for your health and what steps are appropriate.

24-hour Holter

Send your Holter report. Your cardiologist reviews the rhythm over the monitoring period, identifies arrhythmias or ectopic beats, and assesses whether the findings are clinically significant.

Stress test

Send your stress test report. Your cardiologist interprets the functional capacity, haemodynamic response to exercise, and any findings of induced ischaemia.

Blood tests with cardiological markers

If you have recent blood tests with troponins, BNP, NT-proBNP, or a lipid panel, your cardiologist reviews them in the complete clinical context.

To send your tests: upload documents through the platform before the consultation, or send them through the channel the team indicates when you book. Your cardiologist reviews them before the call so the consultation is focused on analysis and planning.

Conditions Commonly Assessed

Heart rhythm disorders

  • Atrial fibrillation — assessment, management, and anticoagulation review in stable presentations
  • Atrial flutter — assessment and management
  • Ectopic beats — assessment of clinical significance and need for intervention
  • Supraventricular tachycardias — assessment and management in non-urgent presentations
  • Bradycardia — assessment of slow rhythm and its clinical significance
  • Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome — review and coordination where indicated

Coronary disease

  • Known and stable ischaemic heart disease — specialist review and treatment optimisation
  • Stable angina — assessment and management
  • Post-myocardial infarction — specialist cardiological follow-up in stable phase
  • Coronary risk assessment — in patients with multiple risk factors

Heart failure

  • Stable heart failure — specialist review and treatment optimisation
  • Review of systolic and diastolic function — echocardiogram interpretation
  • Congestion management — diuretic adjustment and monitoring

Valvular disease

  • Mitral, aortic, tricuspid valvular disease — specialist echocardiogram review and follow-up
  • Assessment of valvular severity — based on echocardiogram report
  • Post-valvular intervention follow-up in stable phase

Hypertension

  • Resistant or poorly controlled hypertension — specialist cardiological assessment
  • Hypertension with organ damage — cardiological impact assessment
  • Global cardiovascular risk review in hypertension

Cardiomyopathies

  • Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy — review and follow-up in stable phase
  • Dilated cardiomyopathy — review and treatment optimisation
  • Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy — assessment and coordination

Cardiovascular risk assessment

  • Global cardiovascular risk assessment — SCORE2 scale, modifiable risk factors
  • Dyslipidaemia with elevated cardiovascular risk — assessment and management plan
  • Metabolic syndrome — cardiological impact assessment
  • Pre-exercise cardiovascular assessment — for adults wanting to start intense physical activity

What Your Consultation Includes

Complete specialist cardiological assessment

Your cardiologist reviews your detailed cardiac history — symptoms, previous episodes, family history of cardiovascular disease, risk factors, current cardiological medication, and available previous investigations.

Specialist test interpretation

Your cardiologist reviews and interprets any cardiological tests you have sent — ECG, echocardiogram, Holter, stress test, blood tests with cardiological markers — providing a clear explanation of the findings and their clinical significance.

Specialist cardiological management plan

Based on the assessment and test interpretation, your cardiologist designs a specialist management plan — which may include cardiological medication adjustment at the specialist's discretion, requests for additional investigations where indicated, and lifestyle and risk factor recommendations.

Specialist clinical documentation — at the specialist's discretion

When clinically indicated, your cardiologist issues appropriate clinical documentation valid at any pharmacy in Spain, as well as specialist reports for continuity of care.

Cardiological investigation requests

Where additional investigations are clinically indicated — ECG, Holter, echocardiogram, blood tests with cardiological markers, stress test — your cardiologist issues the request the same day. Private cardiological testing is available at cardiology clinics and private hospitals throughout Spain.

In-person referral coordination — where indicated

Where in-person assessment, tests that cannot be performed remotely, or cardiological intervention are clinically indicated, your cardiologist coordinates the referral with complete specialist documentation the same day.

Cardiological second opinion

If you have received a cardiological diagnosis, test result, or treatment plan from another cardiologist and want an independent specialist assessment, your cardiologist reviews all available documentation.

Ongoing cardiological follow-up

Specialist follow-up consultations are available for chronic condition monitoring, treatment response review, and interpretation of follow-up investigations.

Cardiology in Spain — The Access Problem

Private cardiology in Spain is well-resourced in Madrid, Barcelona, and other major cities. However, waiting times for a first private cardiologist appointment are generally two to four weeks for non-urgent presentations.

For interpretation of a cardiological test — an ECG with uncertain findings, a Holter that the GP has not been able to fully explain, an echocardiogram with results you do not understand — waiting weeks for a specialist to explain the findings is unnecessarily distressing.

For international residents who need specialist cardiology in English or Portuguese, options are practically non-existent outside Madrid and Barcelona.

Our service provides specialist cardiological assessment with test interpretation the same day — from anywhere in Spain.

Our neurologists, specialist doctors with MIR neurology training, registered with the Spanish Medical Council (OMC — Organización Médica Colegial) and their specialist college, offer specialist neurology consultations by secure video call with neurological imaging and report review — same day, from anywhere in Spain, in English, Spanish, or Portuguese.
serviceTranslations.detailBody:
Who This Service Is For

This specialist neurology consultation is appropriate for adults with:

  • Headache and migraine — diagnosis, treatment planning, preventive medication review, and assessment of treatment-resistant migraine
  • Known and stable epilepsy — antiepileptic medication review, dose adjustment, and ongoing management
  • Chronic vertigo and dizziness — assessment of central or peripheral origin and management plan
  • Stable Parkinson's disease — specialist review and treatment optimisation
  • Stable multiple sclerosis — review and coordination with the hospital team
  • Tremor — essential, postural, or intention — assessment and management
  • Peripheral neuropathy — symptom assessment, electromyogram interpretation, and management plan
  • Restless legs syndrome — assessment and management
  • Mild cognitive impairment — initial assessment, neuropsychological test interpretation, and coordination
  • Cluster headache — diagnosis and management
  • A brain or spinal MRI with findings needing specialist explanation
  • An EEG or electromyogram needing specialist interpretation
  • Specialist neurological second opinion — on a diagnosis, imaging result, or treatment plan
  • International residents and expats who need specialist neurology in English or Portuguese

What This Service Is — And What It Is Not

This specialist neurology consultation covers:

  • Specialist neurological assessment of non-urgent and chronic presentations
  • Review and interpretation of brain and spinal MRI, CT, EEG, and electromyogram
  • Diagnosis and management of the most common neurological conditions seen in outpatient practice
  • Neurological medication review and adjustment
  • Neurological investigation requests where clinically indicated
  • Specialist neurological second opinion
  • Coordination of in-person referral where indicated

This service does not cover:

  • Neurological emergencies — stroke, active seizure, thunderclap headache, acute neurological deficit. For any acute neurological symptom, call 112 immediately
  • Complete neurological examination in all elements — certain components of the neurological examination — deep tendon reflexes, dynamic coordination, detailed sensory testing — require in-person attendance. Your neurologist advises if in-person examination is needed
  • Performing tests — the neurologist can interpret tests already performed and request new ones, but EEG, electromyography, evoked potentials, and lumbar puncture require in-person attendance

Not sure whether your symptom is urgent? For any new or sudden-onset neurological symptom — particularly weakness, loss of sensation, speech or vision disturbance, or sudden severe headache — call 112 immediately. In neurology, time is critical.

Neurological Test Review — How It Works

One of the most valuable capabilities of this service is specialist review and interpretation of neurological tests — the same day, without waiting weeks for an in-person specialist appointment.

Brain and spinal MRI

Send the radiology report of your MRI before the consultation — and if you have the images in digital format, you can also send these. Your neurologist reviews the findings in detail and explains what they mean clinically — whether they are relevant to your symptoms, whether they require follow-up, and whether any further action is needed.

CT scan

Send your CT report. Your neurologist reviews and interprets it in the context of your symptoms and neurological history.

EEG (Electroencephalogram)

Send your EEG report. Your neurologist interprets the findings — whether there is epileptiform activity, whether the trace is normal or has non-specific changes — and contextualises this with your clinical presentation.

Electromyogram (EMG) and nerve conduction study

Send your EMG report. Your neurologist interprets the nerve conduction and muscle activity findings — identifying the pattern of neuropathy, myopathy, or neuromuscular junction involvement — and explains the diagnosis and clinical implications.

Evoked potentials

Send the report. Your neurologist interprets the findings in the context of your clinical presentation — particularly relevant in multiple sclerosis assessment.

To send your tests: upload documents digitally through the platform before the consultation. Your neurologist reviews reports before the call so the consultation is focused on clinical analysis and planning.

Conditions Commonly Assessed

Headache and migraine

  • Episodic migraine — diagnosis, acute treatment and preventive management
  • Chronic migraine — assessment and specialist treatment plan
  • Treatment-resistant migraine — assessment of second-line options including newer migraine-specific therapies
  • Migraine with aura — assessment and management including contraceptive considerations
  • Chronic tension headache — assessment and management
  • Cluster headache — diagnosis and episodic and preventive treatment plan
  • Medication overuse headache — assessment and withdrawal plan
  • Secondary headache — assessment of underlying causes and referral where indicated
  • Trigeminal neuralgia — assessment and management

Epilepsy

  • Known and stable epilepsy — antiepileptic medication review, dose adjustment, and ongoing management
  • First seizure — assessment in non-urgent post-seizure presentations
  • Non-epileptic seizure assessment — differentiation from syncope and psychogenic episodes
  • EEG review in known epilepsy

Movement disorders

  • Stable Parkinson's disease — specialist review and optimisation of dopaminergic treatment
  • Essential tremor — diagnostic assessment and management
  • Dystonia — assessment and treatment plan coordination
  • Restless legs syndrome — assessment and management
  • Tics and Tourette syndrome — assessment and management

Multiple sclerosis

  • Stable multiple sclerosis — review and coordination with the hospital team
  • MRI interpretation in multiple sclerosis
  • Second opinion on MS diagnosis or treatment plan

Vertigo and dizziness

  • Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) — assessment and repositioning manoeuvre guidance
  • Vestibular neuritis — assessment and management
  • Ménière's disease — assessment and management
  • Chronic dizziness — assessment of central or peripheral origin

Peripheral neuropathy

  • Carpal tunnel syndrome — assessment and electromyogram interpretation
  • Diabetic neuropathy — assessment and management
  • Polyneuropathy — diagnostic assessment and electromyogram interpretation
  • Radiculopathy — assessment and management
  • Post-herpetic neuralgia — assessment and management

Cognitive decline

  • Mild cognitive impairment — initial assessment, neuropsychological test interpretation, and coordination
  • Subjective memory complaint — assessment and guidance
  • Second opinion on dementia diagnosis

Sleep and movement

  • Restless legs syndrome — assessment and management
  • Narcolepsy — initial assessment and coordination
  • REM sleep behaviour disorder — assessment and management

What Your Consultation Includes

Complete specialist neurological assessment

Your neurologist reviews your detailed neurological history — symptoms, onset, progression, previous episodes, family history of neurological conditions, current neurological medication, and available previous investigations.

Partial neurological examination by video call

Certain elements of the neurological examination can be assessed by video call — including speech and language evaluation, visible cranial nerves, gross coordination, gait if the patient can show themselves walking, and basic visual fields. Your neurologist guides you on what to do during the call. Where full in-person examination is needed, your neurologist advises clearly.

Specialist neurological test interpretation

Your neurologist reviews and interprets any neurological investigations you have sent — MRI, CT, EEG, electromyogram, evoked potentials — providing a clear explanation of the findings and their clinical significance.

Diagnosis and specialist treatment plan

Based on the assessment, your neurologist establishes the most likely diagnosis or differential diagnoses and designs a specialist treatment plan — including pharmacological options at the specialist's discretion, lifestyle modifications, and coordination of in-person tests or procedures where needed.

Specialist clinical documentation — at the specialist's discretion

When clinically indicated, your neurologist issues appropriate clinical documentation valid at any pharmacy in Spain, as well as specialist reports for continuity of care.

Neurological investigation requests

Where additional investigations are clinically indicated — brain or spinal MRI, CT, EEG, electromyogram, neurological blood tests — your neurologist issues the request the same day.

Neurological second opinion

If you have received a neurological diagnosis, imaging result, or treatment plan from another neurologist and want an independent specialist assessment, your neurologist reviews all available documentation.

In-person referral coordination — where indicated

Where full in-person examination, test performance, or neurological intervention is clinically indicated, your neurologist coordinates referral with complete specialist documentation the same day.

Ongoing neurological follow-up

Specialist follow-up consultations are available for chronic condition monitoring, treatment response review, and interpretation of follow-up investigations.

Migraine — Why It Deserves Specialist Neurological Assessment

Migraine affects approximately 15% of the Spanish adult population and is the second leading cause of neurological disability worldwide. Yet most migraine patients receive suboptimal treatment — frequently because GP-level management cannot access all available therapeutic options.

A specialist neurologist can:

  • Establish the precise diagnosis — differentiating between episodic, chronic, with aura, vestibular, and other migraine variants that have different treatments
  • Optimise acute treatment — selecting the most appropriate triptan for your clinical profile
  • Initiate or review preventive treatment — including first, second, and third-line options, including newer migraine-specific therapies available in Spain
  • Identify and manage medication overuse headache — a common complication in migraineurs who self-medicate
  • Assess cardiovascular risk factors in migraine with aura — important for contraceptive decisions

If your migraines have a significant impact on your life — more than four episodes per month, prolonged duration, poor response to acute treatment, or a recent change in pattern — specialist neurological assessment is the clinically appropriate step.

Neurology in Spain — The Access Problem

Private neurology in Spain is well-resourced in major cities but with waiting times of four to eight weeks for a first private neurologist appointment for non-urgent presentations. In the public system, waiting times are longer still in most autonomous communities.

For international residents who need specialist neurology in English or Portuguese, options are practically non-existent outside Madrid and Barcelona.

For interpretation of neurological imaging — a brain MRI with uncertain findings, an EEG that the GP has not been able to fully explain, an electromyogram with results you do not understand — waiting weeks for a specialist to explain the findings is unnecessarily distressing.

Our service provides specialist neurological assessment with test interpretation the same day — from anywhere in Spain.

serviceTranslations.heroDescription: Some paediatric concerns go beyond what can be addressed in a GP paediatric consultation. A child with severe asthma not responding to standard treatment, a complex chronic paediatric condition, developmental concerns requiring specialist assessment, or a test result that nobody has fully explained — these presentations require the depth of clinical analysis that a specialist paediatrician provides. Our paediatricians, specialist doctors with MIR paediatric training, registered with the Spanish Medical Council (OMC — Organización Médica Colegial) and their specialist college, offer specialist paediatric consultations by secure video call — same day, from anywhere in Spain, in English, Spanish, or Portuguese. A parent or guardian must be present throughout all consultations for children under 16.
serviceTranslations.detailBody:
GP Paediatrics vs. Specialist Paediatrics

Global Health offers two levels of paediatric care.

GP paediatric consultation — appropriate for common acute and non-urgent childhood illnesses: fever, infections, rashes, infant sleep problems, and parental guidance. The right starting point for most day-to-day paediatric concerns.

Specialist paediatric consultation — conducted by specialist paediatricians with MIR training. Appropriate for:

  • Chronic and complex paediatric conditions requiring specialist management
  • Developmental concerns — assessment, coordination, and second opinion
  • Paediatric conditions not responding to GP-level management
  • Specialist paediatric second opinion
  • Specialist review and interpretation of paediatric investigations

Not sure which level is right? Start with the GP paediatric consultation — if your child's presentation requires specialist paediatric assessment, your GP refers you directly to this service within the same platform.

Who This Service Is For

This specialist paediatric consultation is appropriate for children, adolescents, and their families when:

  • The child has a chronic paediatric condition — asthma, type 1 diabetes, paediatric epilepsy, paediatric inflammatory bowel disease, autoimmune conditions — requiring specialist review
  • There are developmental concerns — language, motor, social, or cognitive development — requiring specialist assessment or second opinion
  • The child has complex allergies or severe asthma not responding to standard treatment
  • There are paediatric endocrinological concerns — growth problems, early or delayed puberty, type 1 diabetes
  • There are chronic paediatric gastrointestinal problems — chronic abdominal pain, coeliac disease, severe reflux
  • The adolescent has mental health difficulties — anxiety, depression — requiring specialist paediatric assessment
  • Parents want a second opinion on their child's diagnosis, treatment plan, or investigation result
  • The family is international or expat and needs specialist paediatrics in English or Portuguese
  • Parents received clinical documentation in Spanish about their child that they need explained clearly

Conditions Commonly Assessed

Paediatric respiratory

  • Paediatric asthma — diagnosis, treatment plan review, difficult-to-control asthma assessment, and inhaled medication adjustment
  • Chronic cough in children — underlying cause assessment
  • Recurrent wheeze in infants and young children — assessment and management plan
  • Recurrent bronchitis — assessment and coordination

Allergy and paediatric immunology

  • Food allergy — assessment, allergy test interpretation, and management plan
  • Allergic rhinoconjunctivitis — assessment and management
  • Severe atopic dermatitis — specialist assessment and treatment plan
  • Chronic paediatric urticaria — assessment and management
  • Immunodeficiency — initial assessment and coordination

Development and paediatric neurology

  • Developmental concerns — language delay, motor delay, social communication difficulties
  • Autism spectrum disorder — initial assessment and coordination for formal diagnosis
  • Learning difficulties — assessment and coordination
  • Stable paediatric epilepsy — antiepileptic medication review and ongoing management
  • Paediatric headache and migraine — assessment and treatment plan
  • Paediatric tics and Tourette syndrome — assessment and management

Paediatric endocrinology

  • Growth problems — short or tall stature, growth velocity assessment
  • Early or delayed puberty — assessment and coordination
  • Type 1 diabetes in children — specialist review and treatment optimisation
  • Paediatric hypothyroidism — review and management
  • Paediatric obesity — medical assessment and intervention plan

Paediatric gastroenterology

  • Chronic abdominal pain in children — underlying cause assessment
  • Coeliac disease — diagnosis, management, and follow-up
  • Gastro-oesophageal reflux in infants and children — assessment and treatment plan
  • Chronic paediatric constipation — assessment and management
  • Stable paediatric inflammatory bowel disease — review and coordination

Paediatric mental health

  • Anxiety in children and adolescents — specialist paediatric assessment and care plan coordination
  • Depression in adolescents — specialist paediatric assessment and coordination
  • Sleep disorders in children — specialist assessment and management

Complex paediatric dermatology

  • Severe eczema — specialist assessment and treatment plan
  • Paediatric psoriasis — assessment and management
  • Paediatric alopecia — assessment and coordination

Paediatric second opinion

  • Second opinion on paediatric diagnoses
  • Review of paediatric treatment plans
  • Interpretation of paediatric investigations — blood tests, allergy tests, lung function tests, MRI

What Your Consultation Includes

Complete specialist paediatric assessment

Your specialist paediatrician conducts a full assessment — including detailed paediatric history, developmental review, relevant family history, previous treatments and their response, and review of any available investigations. For younger children, the consultation is conducted with parents describing the situation and showing the child on video where clinically relevant.

Visual and behavioural assessment

Certain aspects of the paediatric assessment can be conducted by video call — including observation of the child's behaviour, language and communication, response to instructions, parent interaction, and visible developmental aspects. Your paediatrician guides you on what to show during the call.

Specialist review of paediatric investigations

Your specialist paediatrician reviews and interprets paediatric investigations — blood tests, allergy tests (skin prick, specific IgE), lung function tests, neuroimaging results, and other investigations — providing a clear explanation of the findings and their clinical significance.

Specialist paediatric diagnosis and treatment plan

Based on the assessment, your paediatrician establishes the most likely diagnosis and designs a specialist treatment plan — including paediatric pharmacological options at the specialist's discretion, non-pharmacological interventions, and coordination with other services where indicated.

Safety assessment

Every paediatric consultation includes assessment of whether the child's presentation requires emergency or urgent in-person care. Your paediatrician advises clearly and immediately if this is the case.

Specialist clinical documentation — at the specialist's discretion

When clinically indicated, your paediatrician issues appropriate clinical documentation — including specialist reports for school, letters for other specialists, and referral letters.

Multidisciplinary coordination

For children with complex conditions requiring multiple specialist input — paediatric neurology, child psychology, speech therapy, paediatric physiotherapy, paediatric nutrition — your paediatrician coordinates the care plan and appropriate referrals the same day.

Ongoing specialist paediatric follow-up

Specialist follow-up consultations are available for chronic condition monitoring, treatment response review, and ongoing paediatric care.

Important Information Before You Book

  • A parent or guardian must be present throughout all consultations for children under 16, in accordance with Organic Law 1/1996 on the Legal Protection of Minors and Law 41/2002
  • For adolescents aged 16 and over, the paediatrician assesses capacity to consent individually — the concept of the "mature minor" under Spanish law
  • Fever in infants under 3 months is a medical emergency — do not book a video consultation
  • Paediatric emergencies — call 112 or go to the nearest paediatric emergency department immediately
  • Mandatory reporting — our paediatricians are bound by mandatory child protection reporting obligations under Organic Law 1/1996. This obligation takes precedence over confidentiality
  • Bring any tests, reports, specialist letters, or relevant clinical documentation about your child to the consultation

Specialist Paediatrics in Spain — The Access Problem

Private specialist paediatrics in Spain is well-resourced in major cities but with waiting times of three to six weeks for a first private specialist paediatrician appointment. In the public system, waiting times are longer still.

For international families who need specialist paediatrics in English or Portuguese, options are practically non-existent outside Madrid and Barcelona.

For chronic paediatric conditions, developmental disorders, or conditions not responding to standard treatment, delay in specialist assessment has direct consequences for the child's development, academic performance, and wellbeing. Fast access to specialist assessment matters.

Our service provides specialist paediatric assessment the same day — from anywhere in Spain.

serviceTranslations.name: Caída del Cabello
serviceTranslations.summary: Un médico busca por videollamada la causa de tu Caída del Cabello o pérdida de densidad y te orienta sobre un manejo basado en la evidencia.
serviceTranslations.seoTitle: Caída del Cabello Online España | Evaluación Médica | Médico de Cabecera
serviceTranslations.seoDescription: ¿Pérdida de cabello o adelgazamiento capilar? Nuestros médicos de cabecera colegiados evalúan la causa médica de tu caída del cabello y asesoran sobre tratamiento basado en evidencia. El mismo día en España.
serviceTranslations.heroTitle: Caída del Cabello — Evaluación Médica Online el Mismo Día
serviceTranslations.heroDescription: La caída del cabello es una de las preocupaciones médicas más comunes — y una de las más frecuentemente ignoradas. La mayoría de las personas que notan una pérdida significativa o adelgazamiento capilar nunca consultan a un médico sobre ello, ya sea porque asumen que no se puede hacer nada, o porque no saben por dónde empezar. Ambas suposiciones son incorrectas. En la gran mayoría de los casos, la caída del cabello tiene una causa médica identificable — y cuanto antes se evalúa, mejor es el resultado. Los folículos pilosos que han estado inactivos durante un período prolongado son significativamente más difíciles de recuperar que los folículos que están adelgazando pero todavía activos. Nuestros médicos de cabecera, colegiados conforme a los requisitos de la Organización Médica Colegial (OMC), ofrecen evaluaciones médicas completas de caída del cabello por videollamada segura — identificando la causa subyacente, asesorando sobre gestión basada en evidencia, y emitiendo la documentación clínica correspondiente donde esté clínicamente indicado. El mismo día, desde cualquier punto de España, en español, inglés o portugués.
serviceTranslations.detailBody:
Por qué la evaluación temprana marca la diferencia

La caída del cabello sigue casi siempre un patrón progresivo — especialmente la alopecia androgénica en hombres y mujeres. El argumento clínico para la evaluación temprana es sencillo: cuanto antes se identifica la causa y se inicia el tratamiento apropiado, mejor es el resultado. Esperar hasta que la caída del cabello sea avanzada reduce significativamente las opciones de tratamiento disponibles.

Si has notado cambios en la densidad de tu cabello, en tu línea capilar o en el patrón de caída — aunque no estés seguro de si es lo suficientemente significativo como para ver a un médico — reserva una consulta. Tu médico te dirá honestamente si la intervención está justificada y cuáles son las opciones.

Para quién es este servicio

Esta consulta es apropiada para adultos que experimentan:

  • Adelgazamiento gradual del cabello en el cuero cabelludo — en hombres o mujeres
  • Retroceso de la línea del cabello o adelgazamiento temporal
  • Adelgazamiento en la coronilla o en la parte superior del cuero cabelludo
  • Caída de cabello repentina o por parches
  • Caída difusa — más cabello en la ducha, en la almohada o en el cepillo
  • Caída del cabello tras un evento vital significativo — enfermedad, cirugía, parto o estrés intenso
  • Caída del cabello asociada a otros síntomas — fatiga, cambios de peso, cambios en la piel o las uñas — que pueden indicar una afección subyacente
  • Afecciones del cuero cabelludo — caspa, seborrea o inflamación que afecta al crecimiento del cabello
  • Caída del cabello que no ha respondido a tratamientos sin receta

Condiciones habitualmente evaluadas

Caída del cabello en hombres

  • Alopecia androgénica — la causa más común de caída del cabello en hombres, evaluada y gestionada a nivel de medicina general incluyendo discusión de opciones de tratamiento basadas en evidencia
  • Alopecia areata — caída del cabello por parches de base autoinmune
  • Efluvio telógeno — caída difusa tras enfermedad, estrés o deficiencia nutricional
  • Dermatitis seborreica e inflamación del cuero cabelludo que contribuyen a la caída del cabello
  • Caída del cabello relacionada con medicamentos — evaluación y gestión

Caída del cabello en mujeres

  • Alopecia androgénica femenina
  • Efluvio telógeno — especialmente posparto, tras enfermedad significativa, o tras estrés importante
  • Alopecia areata
  • Caída del cabello relacionada con cambios hormonales — SOP, disfunción tiroidea, menopausia o cambios hormonales posparto
  • Caída del cabello relacionada con deficiencia nutricional — hierro, ferritina, vitamina D, B12 y zinc
  • Alopecia de tracción — relacionada con prácticas de peinado
  • Caída del cabello relacionada con medicamentos

Ambos

  • Tiña capitis — infección fúngica del cuero cabelludo que causa caída del cabello, que requiere tratamiento
  • Alopecia cicatricial — requiere derivación urgente a dermatología
  • Caída del cabello como síntoma de afecciones sistémicas — enfermedad tiroidea, afecciones autoinmunes, anemia

Qué incluye la consulta

Evaluación completa de la caída del cabello

Tu médico de cabecera revisa el historial de tu caída del cabello en detalle — inicio, patrón, velocidad de progresión, antecedentes familiares, síntomas asociados, medicación actual, estado nutricional, eventos vitales recientes y salud general — construyendo un cuadro completo como base para identificar la causa.

Identificación de la causa subyacente

La caída del cabello es frecuentemente un síntoma de algo sistémico — no solo una preocupación estética. Tu médico de cabecera evalúa los contribuyentes hormonales, nutricionales, autoinmunes y relacionados con medicamentos que pueden estar causando o acelerando tu caída del cabello.

Plan de gestión basado en evidencia

Basándose en la evaluación, tu médico asesora sobre el enfoque más apropiado para tu tipo específico de caída del cabello — que puede incluir optimización nutricional, tratamientos tópicos, recomendaciones clínicas a criterio del médico, y derivación donde esté indicado.

Solicitud de análisis donde esté indicado

Donde los análisis de sangre estén clínicamente indicados — función tiroidea, ferritina, estudios de hierro, panel hormonal, niveles de vitaminas — tu médico los solicita el mismo día.

Documentación clínica — a criterio del médico

Cuando esté clínicamente indicado, tu médico emite la documentación clínica correspondiente válida en cualquier farmacia española.

Nota: Los estupefacientes y determinadas sustancias controladas requieren documentación especial que no puede emitirse electrónicamente. Tu médico te informará si esto aplica.

Derivación a dermatología donde sea necesario

Determinadas afecciones de caída del cabello — incluyendo alopecia cicatricial, alopecia areata compleja, y presentaciones que requieren biopsia del cuero cabelludo — requieren evaluación dermatológica especializada. Tu médico de cabecera te asesora claramente si este es tu caso y coordina la derivación.

Por qué la caída del cabello se descarta con demasiada frecuencia

La caída del cabello se encuentra frecuentemente con "es normal" o "es solo estrés" — a veces correctamente, pero demasiado a menudo sin la investigación adecuada. Un médico que evalúa genuinamente la caída del cabello no empieza con una respuesta genérica. Empieza con una historia completa, evalúa el cuadro hormonal y nutricional, e identifica la causa específica antes de proponer un enfoque adaptado a esa causa.

La diferencia entre "es probablemente estrés" sin investigación y "tu ferritina está baja y esto está causando efluvio telógeno, que es tratable" con un análisis de sangre no es pequeña. Es la diferencia entre una preocupación descartada y una condición identificada y manejable.

serviceTranslations.summary: Erupciones, eccema, acné o una lesión que quieres revisar: en la Consulta de Piel un médico te valora por videollamada y te deriva a dermatología si hace falta.
serviceTranslations.seoTitle: Consulta de Piel Online España | Médico de Cabecera
serviceTranslations.seoDescription: Sarpullido, eccema, acné u otra preocupación de piel. Nuestros médicos de cabecera colegiados evalúan afecciones cutáneas por videollamada segura. Evaluación clínica el mismo día en España.
serviceTranslations.heroTitle: Consulta de Piel — Evaluación Clínica con Médico de Cabecera Online
serviceTranslations.heroDescription: Una erupción nueva, un brote de eccema, acné que afecta tu confianza, o una lesión cutánea que llevas tiempo queriendo revisar. La mayoría de las preocupaciones de piel pueden evaluarse clínicamente por videollamada por un médico de cabecera con experiencia — sin necesidad de esperar semanas para una cita en dermatología. Nuestros médicos de cabecera, colegiados conforme a los requisitos de la Organización Médica Colegial (OMC), ofrecen evaluaciones de piel completas por videollamada segura — identificando tu afección, asesorando sobre gestión basada en evidencia, y derivando a nuestro servicio de dermatología especializada donde se necesite valoración más profunda. El mismo día, desde cualquier punto de España, en español, inglés o portugués.
serviceTranslations.detailBody:
Consulta de piel con médico de cabecera vs. consulta dermatológica especialista

Global Health ofrece dos niveles de atención para afecciones cutáneas:

  • Consulta de piel con médico de cabecera — apropiada para la mayoría de presentaciones cutáneas agudas y no urgentes. Eccema, acné leve a moderado, erupciones, infecciones cutáneas, lunares de vigilancia rutinaria, y afecciones cutáneas crónicas gestionadas a nivel de medicina general. Es el punto de entrada correcto para la mayoría de preocupaciones de piel.
  • Consulta dermatológica especialista — realizada por dermatólogos colegiados de Global Health. Apropiada para afecciones complejas, resistentes al tratamiento, o que requieren valoración especializada — incluyendo acné grave con consideración de isotretinoína, lesiones sospechosas que requieren dermatoscopia de alta resolución, psoriasis compleja, y afecciones que requieren biopsia coordinada.

¿No estás seguro de cuál es el nivel apropiado para tu preocupación? Empieza con la consulta de medicina general — si tu presentación requiere valoración dermatológica especializada, tu médico de cabecera te deriva directamente a nuestro servicio de dermatología dentro de la misma plataforma.

Para quién es este servicio

Esta consulta es apropiada para adultos y niños que presentan:

  • Una erupción, cambio cutáneo o lesión nueva que necesita evaluación clínica
  • Una afección cutánea existente que está en brote o no responde al tratamiento actual
  • Acné leve a moderado — comedonal, inflamatorio o mixto
  • Eccema o dermatitis atópica — evaluación de brote y gestión continuada
  • Psoriasis — presentaciones no complejas a nivel de medicina general
  • Un lunar o lesión cutánea de vigilancia rutinaria
  • Reacciones alérgicas cutáneas — urticaria, dermatitis de contacto o reacciones medicamentosas
  • Afecciones del cuero cabelludo — dermatitis seborreica, psoriasis del cuero cabelludo o afecciones fúngicas
  • Infecciones cutáneas — bacterianas, virales o fúngicas
  • Afecciones cutáneas crónicas gestionadas a nivel de medicina general
  • Pacientes que necesitan una carta de derivación a dermatología

Condiciones habitualmente evaluadas

Condiciones inflamatorias

  • Eccema y dermatitis atópica — gestión de brotes, identificación de desencadenantes, atención continuada
  • Psoriasis — presentaciones no complejas a nivel de medicina general
  • Dermatitis seborreica — presentación en cuero cabelludo y facial
  • Rosácea — evaluación y gestión a nivel de medicina general
  • Dermatitis perioral

Acné

  • Acné leve a moderado — comedonal, inflamatorio y mixto
  • Acné en adolescentes y adultos
  • Acné hormonal en mujeres — evaluado junto con evaluación hormonal donde esté indicado
  • Evaluación de pigmentación postacné y cicatrices
  • Revisión de gestión del acné — pacientes ya en tratamiento que necesitan revisión clínica

El acné grave que pueda requerir isotretinoína necesita valoración por nuestro servicio de dermatología especialista — tu médico de cabecera te deriva directamente si tu presentación lo justifica.

Condiciones alérgicas y reactivas

  • Urticaria — habones agudos y crónicos
  • Dermatitis alérgica de contacto — evaluación y asesoramiento sobre evitación de alérgenos
  • Reacciones medicamentosas que afectan a la piel
  • Angioedema — evaluación y gestión a nivel de medicina general
  • Presentaciones cutáneas de alergia alimentaria

Infecciones

  • Impétigo — infección cutánea bacteriana
  • Celulitis — evaluación y gestión con escalada donde esté indicado
  • Foliculitis
  • Infecciones cutáneas fúngicas — tiña corporal, tiña pedis, tiña versicolor
  • Molusco contagioso
  • Verrugas y verrugas plantares
  • Herpes simple — herpes labial y herpes cutáneo
  • Herpes zóster — evaluación y gestión

Pigmentación y lesiones — vigilancia rutinaria

  • Lunares de vigilancia rutinaria — evaluación clínica y derivación a dermatología especialista donde esté indicado
  • Hiperpigmentación postinflamatoria
  • Melasma — evaluación y gestión
  • Vitíligo — evaluación y derivación donde esté indicado

Las lesiones sospechosas que requieren dermatoscopia o biopsia se derivan a nuestro servicio de dermatología especialista.

Afecciones del cuero cabelludo

  • Dermatitis seborreica del cuero cabelludo
  • Psoriasis del cuero cabelludo — presentaciones no complejas
  • Foliculitis del cuero cabelludo
  • Tiña capitis — infección fúngica del cuero cabelludo

Afecciones cutáneas pediátricas

  • Eccema en lactantes y niños
  • Dermatitis del pañal y preocupaciones cutáneas en lactantes
  • Erupciones virales infantiles — evaluación y orientación para padres
  • Impétigo e infecciones cutáneas en niños
  • Molusco contagioso en niños

Qué incluye la consulta

Evaluación visual clínica

Las afecciones cutáneas son especialmente adecuadas para la videoconsulta — tu médico de cabecera puede observar la lesión, erupción o cambio cutáneo directamente durante la llamada. Una buena iluminación y una vista clara de la cámara mejoran significativamente la calidad de la evaluación — tu médico te guía sobre el posicionamiento durante la llamada.

Historia clínica completa

El médico revisa el inicio, progresión, distribución, síntomas asociados, desencadenantes, tratamientos previos, historial médico relevante, medicación y antecedentes familiares de afecciones cutáneas.

Diagnóstico y plan de gestión

Basándose en la evaluación, el médico asesora sobre el diagnóstico más probable, el enfoque de gestión apropiado, y qué esperar del tratamiento — incluyendo cómo monitorizar tu afección y cuándo buscar revisión adicional.

Documentación clínica — a criterio del médico

Cuando esté clínicamente indicado, el médico emite la documentación clínica correspondiente válida en cualquier farmacia española.

Nota: Los estupefacientes y determinadas sustancias controladas requieren documentación especial que no puede emitirse electrónicamente. Tu médico de cabecera te informará si esto aplica.

Solicitud de análisis donde esté indicado

Donde los análisis de sangre — incluyendo paneles de alergia o marcadores inflamatorios — estén clínicamente indicados, el médico los solicita el mismo día.

Derivación interna a dermatología especialista — donde sea necesario

Donde se requiera evaluación dermatológica especializada — incluyendo lesiones sospechosas, acné grave, afecciones complejas o resistentes al tratamiento — tu médico de cabecera te deriva directamente a nuestro servicio de dermatología especialista dentro de la misma plataforma, el mismo día.

Lunares y lesiones cutáneas — cuándo actuar con prontitud

Cualquier cambio en un lunar o lesión cutánea justifica evaluación clínica. Los criterios ABCDE son la guía clínica estándar:

  • A — Asimetría — una mitad no coincide con la otra
  • B — Borde — bordes irregulares, dentados o difusos
  • C — Color — variación de color dentro de la lesión
  • D — Diámetro — mayor de 6mm
  • E — Evolución — cualquier cambio de tamaño, forma, color, o cualquier síntoma nuevo

Si tu lesión cumple alguno de estos criterios, reserva una evaluación con prontitud. Tu médico de cabecera evalúa visualmente y, donde esté indicado, te deriva directamente a nuestro servicio de dermatología especialista para valoración con dermatoscopia.

Preparación para tu consulta de piel

  • Buena iluminación — la luz natural o una lámpara dirigida a la zona afectada da a tu médico la vista más clara
  • Fotos claras — toma fotos claras de la zona afectada antes de tu consulta
  • Múltiples ángulos — muestra la lesión o erupción desde múltiples ángulos durante la llamada
  • Nota el historial — cuándo empezó, cómo ha cambiado, qué lo mejora o empeora, y qué has probado ya

serviceTranslations.heroDescription: ¿Necesitas ver a un médico hoy pero no tienes médico de cabecera asignado, no puedes esperar semanas para una cita, o simplemente necesitas una consulta médica rápida y de calidad sin desplazarte? Sin registro previo, sin sala de espera, con documentación clínica completa emitida el mismo día desde cualquier punto del país.
serviceTranslations.detailBody:
La realidad del acceso sanitario en España

El sistema sanitario español es uno de los mejores de Europa — pero el acceso tiene fricciones reales para una parte importante de la población.

Si eres autónomo sin médico de cabecera asignado actualmente, si has cambiado de comunidad autónoma recientemente, si llevas semanas esperando cita en el CAP, si necesitas atención hoy y el sistema público no puede dártela, o si prefieres una consulta privada sin las esperas habituales — este servicio existe para ti.

Nuestros médicos colegiados realizan consultas médicas privadas completas por videollamada, con la misma validez clínica y legal que una consulta presencial. La documentación clínica que emiten — incluyendo receta privada electrónica donde esté clínicamente indicado — está conectada a Nodofarma y es válida en las más de 22.000 farmacias del territorio nacional.

¿Ya tienes médico de cabecera en el sistema público? Este servicio funciona como complemento — para cuando necesitas atención hoy y tu CAP no tiene cita disponible, o para una segunda opinión antes de tomar una decisión médica importante.

Para qué podemos ayudarte

Nuestros médicos evalúan y gestionan una amplia gama de problemas de salud agudos y no urgentes:

Respiratorio y ORL

  • Resfriado, gripe, sinusitis y bronquitis
  • Síntomas de COVID-19 y problemas post-COVID
  • Dolor de garganta, amigdalitis e infecciones de oído
  • Infecciones pulmonares y tos persistente
  • Crisis leves de asma

Infecciones

  • Infecciones de orina — evaluación y tratamiento donde esté clínicamente indicado
  • Infecciones cutáneas
  • Infecciones respiratorias que requieren evaluación
  • Infecciones gastrointestinales

General y sistémico

  • Fiebre en adultos
  • Cefaleas y migraña
  • Náuseas, vómitos, diarrea y dolor abdominal
  • Fatiga y malestar general

Piel y ojos

  • Erupciones, eccema y reacciones alérgicas leves
  • Conjuntivitis e irritación ocular leve

Musculoesquelético

  • Dolor de espalda, cervical y muscular
  • Lesiones musculoesqueléticas menores

Otros

  • Dudas sobre medicación actual o tratamiento en curso
  • Documentación médica — justificantes, derivaciones
  • Consejo médico de viaje
  • Segunda opinión sobre diagnósticos o planes de tratamiento

Qué incluye tu consulta

Evaluación clínica completa

El médico recoge una historia clínica completa de tus síntomas, antecedentes médicos relevantes y medicación actual — y realiza una evaluación clínica estructurada por videollamada, con el mismo estándar que una consulta presencial.

Explicación clara

Sales de la consulta sabiendo exactamente qué está ocurriendo, qué debes hacer y cuándo buscar atención adicional. Sin prisa, sin barreras lingüísticas.

Documentación clínica — a criterio del médico

El médico emite la documentación clínica apropiada para tu situación tras evaluación completa. Esto puede incluir receta privada electrónica conforme al Real Decreto 1718/2010, homologada por la OMC y conectada a través de Nodofarma a las más de 22.000 farmacias del territorio nacional — donde esté clínicamente indicado. Presenta tu DNI en cualquier farmacia de tu elección.

La receta privada tiene una validez general de 10 días naturales para la primera dispensación. En tratamientos crónicos, el médico puede programar dispensaciones sucesivas según la duración del tratamiento.

Antibióticos — evaluación y tratamiento donde esté indicado

En España, todos los antibióticos requieren prescripción médica. Tu médico evalúa tus síntomas y prescribe el tratamiento adecuado donde la evidencia clínica lo justifica — incluyendo infecciones de orina, infecciones respiratorias e infecciones cutáneas — siguiendo los principios de uso responsable de antibióticos.

Derivaciones y documentación médica

Cuando se necesita derivación a especialista, analíticas, pruebas de imagen u otra documentación clínica, el médico la emite el mismo día.

Justificante médico

Si necesitas justificar una ausencia laboral, el médico puede emitir el certificado médico correspondiente donde esté clínicamente indicado, tras evaluación completa.

Receta privada electrónica — cómo funciona en España

La receta médica privada electrónica en España está regulada por el Real Decreto 1718/2010 y es válida en todo el territorio nacional. Nuestros médicos emiten recetas privadas electrónicas homologadas por la OMC, conectadas a Nodofarma.

Con una receta privada pagas el 100% del precio del medicamento — los precios de los medicamentos en España están regulados y son generalmente muy asequibles. La medicación está disponible en cualquier farmacia española presentando tu DNI.

La receta privada electrónica no es la misma que la receta de la Seguridad Social. Con receta del SNS podrías tener aportación reducida según tu situación. Si tienes médico de cabecera en el sistema público y necesitas medicación financiada, consulta primero con tu CAP.

Quién utiliza este servicio

  • Autónomos y trabajadores sin médico de cabecera asignado actualmente
  • Personas que han cambiado de comunidad autónoma y aún no tienen CAP asignado
  • Residentes que no pueden esperar semanas para una cita en el sistema público
  • Expats y residentes internacionales que prefieren consultar en inglés o portugués
  • Turistas y nómadas digitales que necesitan atención médica puntual sin seguro español
  • Personas con seguro médico privado que quieren una segunda opinión rápida
  • Cualquiera que necesite un médico hoy sin desplazarse
